verdict: Streaming and studios grew, but legacy TV kept shrinking, so total revenue rose just 1% to $6.91B and profit was a thin $41M after merger-related costs.

segments.name: TV Media
segments.note: CBS, cable networks and TV stations — still the biggest business, but advertising and affiliate fees are shrinking. Shown net of $3M of intersegment eliminations.

segments.name: Direct-to-Consumer
segments.note: Paramount+ and other streaming — revenue rose 9% as Paramount+ added about 2 million subscribers to reach 81.6 million.

segments.name: Studios
segments.note: Paramount Pictures and the TV studios (including Skydance) making films and shows for the company and for others.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Staff, marketing and head-office costs across the studios, networks and streaming services.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Non-cash depreciation and amortization — much higher than the predecessor company after the merger revalued assets.

opex.name: Restructuring & transaction-related items
opex.note: Merger, restructuring and transformation costs from combining Skydance with Paramount.

flow.otherDetail: Other income of -$260M is interest expense of $255M and $34M of other items, minus $29M of interest income. Equity of -$54M is the loss from investee companies (equity-method investments), taken after tax, leaving net earnings of $41M — all of it attributable to the parent in Q2, as noncontrolling interests took $0.

takeaways.title: Streaming is the growth engine
takeaways.text: Direct-to-consumer revenue rose 9% to $2.47B. Paramount+ revenue grew 16%, subscribers reached 81.6 million, and it was the service's best-ever quarter for keeping subscribers.

takeaways.title: Legacy TV keeps shrinking
takeaways.text: TV Media revenue fell 9% to about $3.13B as advertising dropped 14% and pay-TV affiliate fees fell 6%, though tighter costs lifted its profit margin.

takeaways.title: Reported profit is still thin
takeaways.text: Net earnings were just $41M on $6.91B of revenue, after $188M of restructuring and transaction costs and $255M of interest expense. Adjusted EBITDA was $1.1B, up 27%.

oneTimers: Restructuring and transaction-related costs of $188M in the quarter; the shareholder letter says operating income included $153M of transaction-related costs.
The company is preparing a proposed combination with Warner Bros. Discovery, which it flagged as a focus alongside its standalone strategy.
footerNote: Q3 2026 had not been reported as of November 7, 2026, so the latest reported quarter, Q2 2026, is used. This is the merged Paramount Skydance company: Q2 2026 is a full 'successor' quarter (the Skydance merger closed August 7, 2025), so the GAAP income statement is a clean, complete quarter and balances as reported. Year-on-year comparisons are against the 'predecessor' Paramount company, as presented in the release, and segment figures use the company's new TV Media / Direct-to-Consumer / Studios structure, with $3M of intersegment eliminations netted against TV Media so segments sum to total revenue.
